extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism and aspiring prose writers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and evaluative tendencies embedded in Howells's essay about Lowell, useful as guidance for prose diction, revision, critical manners, and the literary author's public/private behavior. Covers stylistic prescriptions, revision habits, attitudes toward publishers/money, and temperamental virtues in criticism and friendship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stickler for best diction
rubrics_metrics.description: He was such a stickler for the best diction that he would not have had me use slovenly vernacular even in the dialogue in my stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insist on precise, elevated wording in prose and dialogue; prefer 'wished' over colloquial 'wanted to.' Example corrections: objected to 'silvern' in 'The silvern chords of the piano trembled' — preferred plain 'silver.' Anti-pattern: affected or showy adjectives ('silvern') that strike the reader as pretentious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation in word choice
rubrics_metrics.description: He objected to affectation in words and would tolerate only words that 'would serve his turn, without wincing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words that feel natural and unforced; avoid archaisms or novel coinages that call attention to themselves. Example: prefer 'silver' to 'silvern.' Anti-pattern: coining awkward adjectives for show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision: accept first drafts but allow cooling-off
rubrics_metrics.description: He wrote his poems at a heat, and the manuscript which came to me for the magazine was usually the first draft, very little corrected. But if the cold fit took him quickly it might hold him so fast that he would leave the poem in abeyance till he could slowly live back to a liking for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's acceptable to send strong first drafts; still allow time when enthusiasm dies to step away and return later for revision. Anti-pattern: forcing immediate 'fixes' during a cold fit rather than letting perspective return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be magnanimous and generous in criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: He was most cordial in his recognition of the things that pleased him; nothing I did to his liking failed to bring me a spoken or oftener a written acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating peers, be prompt and generous with positive acknowledgment. Cultivate a habit of written or spoken praise; this is valued over broad popularity. Anti-pattern: withholding praise or being sparing in encouragement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and tolerance toward tiresome or vulgar elements
rubrics_metrics.description: He was often wonderfully patient of tiresome people, and sometimes celestially insensible to vulgarity. One of the dangers of scholarship was a peculiar danger in the Cambridge keeping, but Lowell was almost as averse as Longfellow from contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contempt and sneering; tolerate imperfect manners and vulgarity without derision. Anti-pattern: snubbing or sneering at perceived inferiority or presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sneering; snub only presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: He could snub, and pitilessly, where he thought there was presumption ... but I cannot remember ever to have heard him sneer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish legitimate correction of presumption from mean-spirited sneer; aim for firm correction without scorn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive to apparent fading of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the modesty that is always a quality of such a nature, he was magnanimously sensitive to the appearance of fading interest; he could not take it otherwise than as a proof of his fading power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and respect authors' anxieties about waning attention; when curating or publishing, be mindful of feelings that omission may cause. Anti-pattern: thoughtless omission of an author's name from a prospectus without explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance scholarship with literary feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: He would not have had me too learned, holding that he had himself been hurt for literature by his scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting scholarship or excessive learning overshadow the literary vitality of a work; prioritize emotional and aesthetic effects over pedantic displays of learning. Anti-pattern: making literature too scholarly at the expense of life and feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for publishers' commercial choices (titles/marketing)
rubrics_metrics.description: He wished to name these more soberly, but at the urgence of his publishers he gave them titles which they thought would be attractive to the public, though he felt that they took from the dignity of his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may compromise on titles or marketing choices for broader appeal; weigh dignity against reach and accept editorial/business input when appropriate. Anti-pattern: refusing any compromise that impedes publication or readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary money ethic: treat earnings as sacred
rubrics_metrics.description: He felt a sacredness in the money got by literature ... which made him wish to dedicate it to something finer than the every day uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may view literary income as special and prefer to spend or dedicate it to lofty ends; this ethic can shape negotiations and requests. Anti-pattern: treating literary payments as purely commercial without attendant moral sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitality and practical help to fellow writers
rubrics_metrics.description: His willingness ... attested in his asking a brother man of letters who wished to work up a subject in the college library, to stay a fortnight in his house, and to share his study, his beloved study, with him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical supports (shared workspace, time, mentorship) are valued contributions to the literary community. Anti-pattern: hoarding resources or refusing to assist less-established writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful line-by-line editorial criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: He would go carefully over a poem with me, word by word, and criticise every turn of phrase, and after all be magnanimously tolerant of my sticking to phrasings that he disliked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to do minute verbal analysis for a colleague's work but accompany it with tolerance for authors' choices. Anti-pattern: heavy-handed imposition of one's wording without allowance for authorial intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'public-school English' constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: He would by no means suffer: 'And what she would, would rather that she would not' ... He said that the stress falling on the last word made it 'public-school English.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to awkward rhythmic stress or didactic/formulaic turns of phrase that sound contrived; revise to naturalize rhythm and diction. Anti-pattern: maintaining stilted or overly formal constructions that call attention to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste: broadly catholic but prone to overvalue touches of life/humor
rubrics_metrics.description: He was of a very catholic taste; and he was apt to be carried away by a little touch of life or humor, and to overvalue the piece in which he found it; but, mainly his judgments of letters and men were just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate wide-ranging taste and be open to small vivid moments, but beware overvaluing pieces solely for a single striking touch. Anti-pattern: letting a single anecdote or humorous line unduly inflate overall judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic sympathy over realism preference
rubrics_metrics.description: He was, by nature and tradition, thoroughly romantic, and he could not or would not suffer realism in any but a friend. He steadfastly refused even to read the Russian masters ... the French naturalists he abhorred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that personal taste (romantic vs. realist) will shape reading and judgment; be explicit about such biases when critiquing. Anti-pattern: total rejection of whole movements without engagement or qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain friendship and avoid letting differences rupture relations
rubrics_metrics.description: He had a most beautiful and endearing ideal of friendship; he desired to affirm it and to reaffirm it as often as occasion offered ... It did not matter what you said or did that contraried him; if he thought he had essentially divined you, you were still the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acting as critic or colleague, prioritize sustaining affectionate, forgiving relations; avoid exacting reciprocity or escalating disagreements into permanent rifts. Anti-pattern: using critical disagreement as a reason to withdraw personal regard.
